title: Nine Days of Water
subtitle: 骆驼与沙漠 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 骆驼与沙漠（自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：骆驼与沙漠（自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：camel　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 camel 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my mother was sent to load ① a camel she could not ride, and she said the riding was the whole of the lesson. The ② camel, meaning the animal and not the load, was nine days from water and was led by whoever came last; a camel, she said, is the only thing in a desert that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ camel in that train had the same bell, and the ④ camel at the end, meaning the one the driver kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever loaded properly. A camel, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ camel was the whole of the crossing, meaning the journey it carried and not the animal. The ⑥ camel, meaning the crossing and not any of that, is the only thing in a desert that everybody trusts and nobody questions; a camel, he said, is either something you load or the only word that means both an animal and a crossing. She said the crossing is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ camel had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the bell. The ⑧ camel of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine days of water and eleven years of loading; a camel, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ camel I remember is the one at the end, which was sold in 1969 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ camel, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being trusted; every camel, she said, is a crossing that has agreed to look like an animal. She said the crossing was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 骆驼（指那头牲口本身，与货物相对）
C. 固定搭配：load a camel 给骆驼装货
D. n. 骆驼（指驼队里每一头）
E. n. 骆驼（指末尾那一头）
F. n. 骆驼（抽象：它所承载的那次穿越）
G. n. 那次穿越（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a camel she could not ride
The camel, meaning the animal and not the load
camel was the whole of the crossing
the camel had become a photograph in a report
The camel of the whole thing
A camel, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: load a camel 意为“给骆驼装货”，1947 年母亲被派去给一头她骑不上的骆驼装货。
camel 意为“骆驼”，指那头牲口本身而不是货物，离水源有九天路，由最后走的人牵着。
camel 指驼队里每一头骆驼，每一头都是同样的铃。
camel 指末尾那一头（赶驼人留的那一头），是唯一有人认真装过货的。
camel 意为“骆驼”，抽象指它所承载的那次穿越，父亲说 camel 就是那次穿越的全部。
camel 为抽象用法，指那次穿越本身，是沙漠里人人都信、却没人质疑的东西。
camel 意为“骆驼”，到 1964 年这头 camel 成了报告里的一张照片。
camel 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九天的水和十一年的装货。
camel 意为“骆驼”，我记得的是末尾那一头，1969 年卖掉，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
camel 为抽象总称，祖母说骆驼是唯一会因为被信任而变好的东西。
